benchmarks.source: AI-DC-FLEX-BENCH-002 / public trace adapters to be pinned
benchmarks.baseline: independent-site aggregation versus empirical joint time series and declared factor/state-space alternatives
benchmarks.target: calibrated held-out aggregate ramp/variance/tail forecasts; reserve must cover measured common-mode and synchronized-release risk

benchmarks.baseline: compute opportunity cost versus BESS/UPS/thermal storage/generator/network alternative
benchmarks.target: compare compute, BESS/UPS and thermal alternatives only after service equivalence; use annualized fixed cost, expected variable cost and lower-bound net delivered MWh; publish break-even compute opportunity cost per event

benchmarks.baseline: cooling-shift/thermal-storage strategy with coolant, temperature, water, auxiliary and recovery constraints
benchmarks.target: compare against fixed-parasitic cooling and coupled electro-thermal baselines; no thermal/water violations

benchmarks.baseline: operational cross-data-centre migration; response ordering depends on replication/remote access/on-demand copy, prelaunch and RO/RW semantics
benchmarks.target: reproduce response ordering; claim strictest evaluated class only for pre-launched RO variants if measurements support it

benchmarks.baseline: 256-GPU-class field demonstration; 25% import/power reduction sustained 3h with declared AI QoS
benchmarks.target: reproduce under matched workload, hardware class, measurement boundary and QoS; stretch >=30% for 3h

benchmarks.source: IEEE workload-driven power fluctuation and data-centre interconnection studies; utility profiles to be pinned
benchmarks.baseline: no-flexibility, independent-site and correlation-aware load cases; local protection stays authoritative
benchmarks.target: no degradation outside operator-approved envelopes; validated RMS/EMT and HIL receipts before any field stability claim

benchmarks.baseline: product-specific latency, sustained delivery, ramp, overshoot and signed under-delivery envelope
benchmarks.target: repeated-call reliability and product-defined response/stability thresholds; no universal threshold invented

benchmarks.baseline: 32 sessions on 8-GPU H100/B200 nodes plus 40 RTX 3060 sessions; >1.8M samples; 15-minute sessions; 20ms node and 100ms single-machine samples
benchmarks.target: use for per-GPU and GPU-sum node characterization only after license review; keep H100, B200 and RTX 3060 strata separate; never label GPU-sum node power as PCC
scope_limits: 15-minute sessions do not qualify a 3-hour sustained field response
H100/B200 data is GPU-sum node power, not facility PCC power
RTX 3060 single-machine scope is not equivalent to a hyperscale facility
no ambient/cooling plant ground truth in the published trace
within-node synchronized GPU patterns are not cross-site dependence evidence
no dataset file is copied into Symtropy while the licence conflict is unresolved

license_evidence.figshare_record: CC BY 4.0 displayed on the DOI landing page
license_evidence.action: obtain author/licensor clarification before commercial use, derivative redistribution or committing dataset-derived artifacts

benchmarks.baseline: 1841 submissions across 60 systems; tokens/J and samples/J
benchmarks.target: first match best eligible result in identical hardware/model/precision/quality stratum; stretch >=5% improvement without quality loss

benchmarks.baseline: linear gain-offset correction, covariance propagation, clock/quality/calibration validity and signed interval energy
benchmarks.target: zero false passes when lower bound misses threshold; no hidden interpolation; every pass bound to calibration and timebase evidence

benchmarks.baseline: PRAS 0.9.0; initial pinned harness 42/42 passing assertions
benchmarks.target: native ELCC method, matched seeds, repeated Monte Carlo, weather-year mixture, tail convergence and multi-region deliverability sensitivities

benchmarks.baseline: up to 22% load deferral in one-week trace-based case; >1M task records
benchmarks.target: reproduce published filters and windows; stretch >=25% only with no SLA, queue, energy/work or rebound regression

benchmarks.baseline: separate no-dispatch calibration and evaluation groups; block-minimum residual calibration; lower-bound holdout coverage and no-dispatch false-positive reduction rate
benchmarks.target: zero future-information leakage; calibration/evaluation groups disjoint; per-regime holdout coverage above pre-registered minimum; false-positive reduction rate <=1% stretch; no event claim without declared recovery horizon

benchmarks.baseline: sum of marginal per-site event success rates and independence assumptions versus observed complete portfolio outcomes grouped by independent stress incident
benchmarks.target: 100% asset-event and domain-event panel completeness; preserve asset response and domain-state provenance; independent incident-group pass rates and worst group shortfall reported separately from dispatch-event pass rates

benchmarks.source: GRID-LOC-DELIV-001 #3826; implementation PR #3827; IEA Electricity 2026 Grids; ESIG Large Loads RA April 2026
benchmarks.baseline: frozen topology and explicit PCC-bus binding, MVA base, branch reactance/rating, chronological injection trace and explicit N-1 outage set
benchmarks.target: 100% known-truth PTDF/flow agreement within declared tolerance; 100% fail-closed for stale topology/islanding/missing mapping; no DC screening result promoted to AC feasibility or N-1 capability
benchmarks.claim_ceiling: linear active-power DC screening only; not AC voltage/reactive feasibility, protection, RMS/EMT, distribution hosting capacity, market accreditation or ELCC

benchmarks.source: GRID-DISTURBANCE-001 #3851; ESIG 2026 large-load modeling/disturbance/performance reports; CIGRE C4-10506-2026; NERC Large Loads Action Plan
benchmarks.baseline: frozen operator-specific voltage/frequency/RoCoF envelope, PCC waveform digest and measurement-chain limits
benchmarks.target: 100% boundary-fixture agreement; zero involuntary trips classified as intentional DR; fail closed on critical gaps, stale requirement and invalid timebase; no sub-cycle/EMT claim from RMS traces
benchmarks.claim_ceiling: observable PCC RMS trace conformance only; not converter internal stability, positive-sequence/EMT model validity, protection, harmonic compliance, interconnection certification, market accreditation or ELCC

result_requirements.hard_gate_policy: Safety, service, metrology and deliverability failures cannot be offset by improvements in another metric.

claim_boundaries: a trace-model result is not field evidence
a grid-facing import reduction is not necessarily facility energy efficiency
a copperplate adequacy pass is not nodal deliverability
a successful PRAS run is not NTCSA model reproduction
MLPerf tokens-per-joule is not grid-service qualification
a k-factor is not a universal confidence level
a software evaluator does not certify instrument transformers or grid-code compliance
the 15-minute H100/B200/RTX workload dataset is component/node evidence, not a facility PCC or three-hour field-response trace
a lower prediction bound calibrated on no-dispatch holdout data is model-based M&V, not causal identification or a joint event-horizon probability bound
the Figshare landing page and accompanying GitHub README report different licences for the high-resolution workload dataset; treat rights as unresolved until clarified by the rights holder
portfolio joint-delivery reports are empirical observed incident-panel results; event count and independent incident-group count are separate
failure-domain membership and state are descriptive observations, not causal failure attribution
overlapping failure-domain capacities must not be summed; V0.1 reports maximum single-domain capacity share rather than an unsupported HHI
site-meter response, network-deliverable response and probabilistic adequacy contribution are three different quantities
DC PTDF/LODF screening is not AC power-flow feasibility, distribution feeder validation, protection coordination or dynamic stability
N-0 deliverability cannot be promoted to N-1 firm deliverability without explicit contingency validation
uncommanded load trip during a voltage/frequency disturbance is not intentional demand response and must not earn flexibility credit
PCC RMS trace conformance does not prove sub-cycle converter stability, harmonic compliance or EMT model validity
disturbance performance is a separate qualification axis from dispatch flexibility
uncommanded load trip during a voltage/frequency disturbance is not intentional demand response and must never earn flexibility credit
PCC RMS trace conformance does not prove sub-cycle converter stability, harmonic compliance, unbalanced-fault response or EMT model validity
disturbance performance is a separate qualification axis from dispatch flexibility
a trace conformance requirement that includes reactive power or current must fail closed when the corresponding required measurement channels are missing
measurement bandwidth cannot exceed the observable Nyquist bandwidth implied by the declared sample cadence
